column1: # LOM_UI_EN faction tips: sects, clans and other factions whose names in dialogue and choices show a short description.
# TAB-separated columns: id, title, forms, description. Lines starting with '#' are comments.
#   id           short name for this list (not shown)
#   title        the name shown at the top of the tip; always matched
#   forms        more name forms matched for it, comma-separated; all matching is case-sensitive and whole-word, and the
#                longest form in a text wins
#   description  the tip's text: who they are, as the story introduces them. Never events, fates or secrets.

column4: Your own sect: the world's foremost masters of hidden weapons and poison, based in Shu, with inner and outsider disciples.
One of the Wulin's Three Great Families, based in Jiangling; renowned for its wide connections, elegant fan techniques, and long-lived elders.
One of the Wulin's Three Great Families, a Fuzhou clan whose ambitious trading and shipping business made it wealthy and far-reaching.
An ancient sect on Mount Kongtong blending martial arts of the Central Plains, Western Xia, and Tubo, organized into four branch gates.
Kongtong Sect's leading branch, said to head its four gates; its disciples pursue immortal cultivation alongside their martial arts.
A Kongtong branch charged with night patrols and hunting down criminals; its unconventional hours and methods unsettle other sects.
A Kongtong branch of smiths and laborers (forging, farming, brewing) trained in tough, hard-hitting fighting styles.
A Kongtong branch focused on internal cultivation; its leader also serves as the sect's archivist and record-keeper.
A Daoist sect whose priests may marry, unlike the celibate Quanzhen; known for Taiji-based inner arts and for driving out evil spirits.
An all-female sect known for elegant swordsmanship, whose disciples often wander the realm righting wrongs.
A sect on Mount Diancang famed for swordsmanship, with a mountain library of sword manuals passed down through generations.
The martial world's largest sect by numbers, made up of wandering beggars organized into branches across the realm.
The government of the Great Song; the Jianghu's martial artists generally keep it at a wary distance.
One of the Six Great Sects; known for its leg techniques, with many members who study Buddhism without taking monastic vows.
An unorthodox cult based at the Six Paths Gorge near Xiangyang, regarded as the gravest danger facing the Wulin in this era.
In the Jianghu, this name is given to whichever unorthodox cult poses the era's greatest threat; every generation has had one.
A local gang known for repeated clashes with the Tang Clan's disciples over the years.
A Daoist order of celibate priests with temples across the realm, teaching internal Qi-cultivation; open to all, though true mastery is rare.
A cult from a past era, once the martial world's greatest threat, destroyed by an alliance of righteous sects and clans.
A gang active in Fujian, skilled with the blade.
Pirates who roam the eastern seas.
A shadowy organization that trains assassins from childhood; its killers operate under inherited code names.
A Buddhist sect centered on Songshan Temple, whose monks study Chan teachings and fist techniques; it keeps a branch in Fujian.
Kongtong, Qingcheng, Emei, Diancang, Songshan, and Quanzhen: the six most prominent orthodox sects in the Wulin.
Tang Clan, Nangong Family, and Shangguan Family: the three most prominent great families in the Wulin.
A coalition of the Wulin's righteous factions, led by an elected Wulin Alliance Leader.
